findings.finding: The service-revenue guide ('at prior-year level', EUR 3,661.8m) is the one line of the 2026 guide still exposed: H1 printed -1.1%, the company-compiled consensus already sits at EUR 3,631.8m for FY (-0.8%) and EUR 913.8m for Q3 (-0.8% y/y), so H2 needs about +1.1% y/y to meet the guide, and a wording trim to 'slightly below' is the main downside path in the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide confirmed at each 2025-26 print; moves on those days were -0.23% (2025-11-11), +2.65% (2026-03-19), 0.0% (2026-05-12), +6.5% (2026-08-06, guide confirmed after the April tariff redesign). An EBITDA guide update by ad-hoc on 2025-06-27 moved -0.85% the next session. Yahoo daily closes.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the analysts' FY number is already 0.8% below the guide, so a trim confirms what is modelled. What is not priced is the company saying so; if it were, the stock would not be trading 14% above its 60-day level near the top of the PT range for the Neutral half (UBS 26.10, Kepler 23).

findings.finding: 1&1 raised DSL and fibre prices for existing customers by EUR 3 a month (about +8.6%, e.g. DSL 250 from 34.99 to 37.99) from October 2026, which supports Q4 service revenue and the 2027 +EUR 100m EBITDA outlook, at the cost of a three-month special-termination window under section 57 TKG.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior isolated reaction; the April 2026 mobile tariff redesign cost 100k contracts and the stock still rose 6.5% at H1 on margin.
findings.original_quote: 1&1 hebt die monatliche Grundgebühr vieler DSL- und Glasfasertarife um drei Euro an, beim Einsteigertarif 1&1 DSL 250 von 34,99 auf 37,99 Euro. Der Aufschlag von gut acht Prozent gilt ab Oktober 2026 und betrifft ausschließlich Bestandskunden, nicht Neuabschlüsse. (1&1 is raising the monthly base fee of many DSL and fibre tariffs by EUR 3, the entry tariff DSL 250 from 34.99 to 37.99. The increase of a good 8% applies from October 2026 and only to existing customers, not new contracts.)
findings.why_not_priced: It sits in the German consumer press, not the investor material; the Q3 consensus has broadband at +7k q/q and FY service revenue still below guide, so nobody has visibly modelled a Q4 price step. If it were in the numbers, Q4-implied service revenue in the consensus would be at or above the guide.

findings.finding: The ~EUR 60m restructuring charge lands in Q3 reported EBITDA (company-compiled consensus EUR 142.0m, -15.8% y/y). The company has said the Visible Alpha consensus does not fully reflect it, so wire headlines comparing to that number may print a large 'miss' that the company has already explained.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ad-hoc announcing the charge (2026-09-10, 19:00) was followed by a 0.0% move on 2026-09-11 (Yahoo close 24.00 both days).
findings.original_quote: Bitte beachten Sie, dass wir im dritten Quartal im Segment „Enterprises & Networks“ einmalige Restrukturierungskosten in Höhe von rund 60 Millionen Euro verbuchen, was sich im „ausgewiesenen“ EBITDA (Gesamt) niederschlägt, während das „bereinigte“ EBITDA unsere operative Leistung widerspiegelt. Dies spiegelt sich nicht vollständig im Konsens von Visible Alpha wider (Please note we book one-off restructuring costs of about EUR 60m in Q3 in Enterprises & Networks, which shows in reported EBITDA, while adjusted EBITDA reflects operating performance. This is not fully reflected in the Visible Alpha consensus.)
findings.why_not_priced: The charge itself is priced (no move on the ad-hoc). What may not be is a mechanical or retail reaction to a headline against a consensus the company says is stale, on a stock where a few thousand shares set the opening print (3,157 shares traded by the 2026-11-11 seal).

findings.finding: United Internet holds 89.32% after the October capital increase, about 1.4m shares below the 90% merger squeeze-out threshold, and has had a standing order to buy up to 6m shares since 2026-08-17 against a free float of about 22.7m shares. That gives a persistent bid under any negative reaction, and a small chance that UI's own Q3 release the same day says something about the stake.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buy-order disclosure moved +8.34% on 2026-08-18; the in-kind capital increase with no premium moved -3.51% on 2026-10-06 (Yahoo closes).
findings.original_quote: Interessewahrende Order zum Kauf von insgesamt bis zu 6.000.000 Aktien der 1&1 AG zu marktschonenden Konditionen im Zeitraum von 17. August 2026 bis 30. Juni 2027. (Order to buy up to 6,000,000 1&1 shares in total, on market-friendly terms, between 17 August 2026 and 30 June 2027.)
findings.why_not_priced: The squeeze-out idea is public (stock3, 2026-10-06), and the stock trades just above the EUR 24.05 issue price, so a squeeze-out premium is not in the price: the October capital increase was sold off. What is not priced is the asymmetry on results day, when a buyer of up to 6m shares stands in a book that trades tens of thousands a day.

findings.finding: The EUR 850.2m loan claim on 1&1 Versatel was converted into equity at EUR 24.05 a share (20% dilution, no cash). That removes the interest on the loan and raises the equity ratio, which the company says is for further network build. The Q3 statement is the first print after the resolution, and the money goes to deleveraging rather than distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: -3.51% on 2026-10-06, the session after the ad-hoc.
findings.why_not_priced: The dilution was priced on 2026-10-06. The interest saving and lower net debt only become visible when the company reports them, and the compiled consensus carries no EPS or net-debt line to show that anyone has updated.

baseline_tension: The lean is -0.105 from the run-up and there is no short anchor. The evidence is close to balanced, with a slight upward tilt from the parent's standing bid and a slight downward one from the service-revenue guide, so it neither confirms nor cuts against the lean in any size that matters.
language_note: The German United Internet Directors' Dealings filing (2026-08-17) carries the 6m-share standing buy order and its end date of 2027-06-30; the English search result list only showed the German title.

The German IR-page note says the ~EUR 60m one-off is booked in Q3 in E&N and that the Visible Alpha consensus does not fully reflect it. I found this in the German page text, not in any English wire item.
The October 2026 broadband price increase for existing customers (+EUR 3 a month) appears only in the German consumer press (drweb.de), not in English sources or company material I could find.
The German squeeze-out framing (stock3: about 1.4m shares short of the threshold) had no English counterpart.
lessons_applied: 'A German ad-hoc filed before the print may have pre-released the number' and 'a finding about a number the market has been told is worth 0': the Q3 one-off finding moves from -0.2 to -0.1, because the September ad-hoc and the company's own consensus note pre-explain it

'Size the move on what is new; let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': abs_move_pct goes from 2.8 to 3.2. The Q3 numbers are new, but the guide is likely only reiterated, so it stays below the 7% new-numbers base. The draft had been anchored on this name's small results-day moves
'In a live bid, results are noise': checked and not applied. UI has a standing market buy order, but there is no offer period, so the results are not overridden
